correctness.rationale: With DFS Phi(lambda,theta)=(sin theta cos lambda,sin theta sin lambda,cos theta), the near-pole torus measure is dx/(|x|sqrt(1-|x|²)) up to finite multiplicity; derivatives of Phi are bounded. For each integer k, chain rule and Frank--Seiringer fractional Hardy at N=2,p=2,sigma=1/2 control weighted L² derivatives of chart functions by source H^(k+1/2), and on nonsingular charts standard Sobolev pullback suffices. Hilbert-scale interpolation yields every real target t>=0 and monotonic Sobolev inclusion all s>=t+1/2. Polar annular bump f_epsilon=epsilon^(s-1)h(dist/epsilon) has bounded sphere H^s norm, while torus H^t norm is bounded below by c epsilon^(s-t-1/2), diverging for s<t+1/2. Exact torus Fourier coefficient normalization (2pi)^-2 and poles/periodic patches are compatible. Verified exact Hardy hypotheses in primary paper, inspected full RESULT.md and check_scaling.py, and independently checked dimensional scaling. The finite scaling script only illustrates the analytic proof.
